answer: Each identity needs a unique issuance signal from an outside attestor; one real-world anchor backs only one signal, so a reused credential is refused. Accounts sealed in a closed island of sibling wallets are flagged, since honest users connect outward while a sybil farm huddles inward. Each epoch a sparrow probe demands a fresh signature, proving a distinct live operator. A thousand aliases then need a thousand external signals and a thousand timely sparrow replies, not one island; every extra identity adds cost until mass forging loses while one honest identity clears every gate.
